title: Offline signed bundles: GA criteria, rollout stages, customer comms, and support readiness
creator: Naomi Feldman
project: Redwood Private – On-prem offline artifact signing
description:
Problem / Why this matters
Air-gapped and offline customer environments cannot rely on online integrity checks or artifact fetching. Today, Redwood Private offline bundles can be modified in transit (intentionally or accidentally) without a deterministic, enforceable verification gate during install/upgrade. This blocks multiple regulated/defense/healthcare opportunities and increases supply-chain risk.

This ticket defines the product release plan for moving signed offline bundles from pilot to GA, including:
- GA criteria (functional + non-functional)
- Rollout stages (pilot → limited availability → GA)
- Customer communication plan (what we tell customers, when, and where)
- Support readiness checklist (runbooks, troubleshooting, escalation, break-glass)

Scope
- Private (VPC + on-prem) offline installation/upgrade bundles.
- Installer preflight signature verification that fails closed by default.
- Key rotation and trust store update flow suitable for air-gapped environments.
- Audit/audit-export readiness for verification outcomes.

Out of scope
- Customer-signed bundles / custom trust root delegation beyond documented future plan.
- Refactoring overall packaging system beyond the bundle/installer changes required for signing/verification.

Definitions
- Pilot: customer-by-customer enablement with Redwood hands-on support; we may ship RC bits and iterate.
- Limited Availability (LA): generally available to Private customers upon request; support + docs considered “stable”, but we may gate by installer version and known environment constraints.
- General Availability (GA): default for all Redwood Private offline bundles; release train gating prevents unsigned artifacts from shipping (except via documented exception/break-glass).

GA entry criteria (must-have)
1) Security & integrity
- Offline bundles include a canonical manifest with hashes for all included artifacts (installer, charts/manifests, image references, runtime/model artifacts, SBOM pointer where available).
- Manifest signature verification occurs during installer preflight and blocks install/upgrade on:
  - invalid signature
  - manifest tampering
  - missing/unknown/untrusted signing key (unless explicit policy-gated break-glass is used)
  - hash mismatch between manifest and on-disk artifacts
- Downgrade/replay protection: installer prevents installing a bundle with a version older than recorded install state unless an explicit rollback path is used (and is logged).
- Key custody meets Redwood security policy: signing keys protected, auditable access, key ceremony evidence captured.

2) Customer experience (air-gapped realities)
- Clear, actionable error messages with stable error codes (supportable at scale).
- Verification can run without outbound network and without requiring system time to be perfectly correct; time-skew handling documented (and diagnostics supported).
- A “bundle inspect” command exists for customers/support to verify signature + show versions before attempting install.

3) Operational readiness
- Release train gating: Private releases cannot ship offline bundles unless signing + verification tests pass (except via approved exception).
- Runbooks and escalation: Support has a documented playbook for verification failures (hash mismatch, unknown key, time skew, downgrade attempt) including what logs to collect.
- Audit logging: verification success/failure events are written locally; export mapping exists for customers with SIEM forwarding.
- Key rotation readiness: documented procedure, and at least one rotation drill completed with lessons incorporated.

4) Documentation & enablement
- Public/private docs: updated installation guide for signed bundles, FAQ/common errors, key rotation/trust store update guide.
- Solutions Engineering enablement: pilot checklist, preflight commands, customer handoff template.

GA exit criteria (launch checklist)
- Two (2) successful pilot customers complete:
  - initial offline install with signed bundle
  - offline upgrade with signed bundle
  - at least one induced failure test in customer-like environment (tampered file / wrong key / hash mismatch) and correct fail-closed behavior verified
- Support readiness sign-off from Support readiness lead (Dev Patel) and SRE sign-off for release gating/alerts (Sean Gallagher).
- Security sign-off from Security Eng lead (Marcus Lin) and GRC mapping confirmed (Olga Petrov / Daniel Carter).

Rollout plan
Phase 1: Pilot (target: Dec 2025 – Jan 2026)
- Enable 2–3 air-gapped customers with Redwood-led execution.
- Requirements:
  - Known-good installer version pinned
  - Support + SE on call for first install window
  - Collect verification/audit logs locally and validate support bundle includes bundle metadata
- Deliverables:
  - Pilot feedback notes
  - Updates to error messages and docs

Phase 2: Limited Availability (target: late Jan – Feb 2026)
- Available to Redwood Private customers “on request” through SE/Support.
- Requirements:
  - Release notes published
  - Docs + troubleshooting stable
  - Key rotation procedure published
  - Known limitations documented (e.g., supported OS tooling for unzip/transfer, time-skew guidance)
- Guardrails:
  - Break-glass requires explicit support workflow and produces audit markers

Phase 3: GA (target: Feb 2026 Private release)
- Signed offline bundles become the default.
- Release gating enforced.
- Exception process documented for emergency unsigned hotfix (approval matrix + customer comms).

Customer communication plan
Audience segments
1) Existing Private customers using offline bundles
- Message: Signed bundles are now standard; install/upgrade will require installer version >= X; verification is enforced; trust store updates required on/after key rotation.
- Channels: release notes, direct email to customer security/platform contacts via CSM/SE, and support KB.

2) Air-gapped prospects in active security review
- Message: Redwood provides cryptographically signed offline bundles with fail-closed verification, local audit trails, and key rotation procedures suitable for air-gapped environments.
- Channels: SE security packet, GRC questionnaire responses, calls.

3) Internal (Support/SE/CS)
- Message: New verification steps, common failures, required logs, and escalation process.
- Channels: internal enablement doc + office hours.

Comms content requirements (draft bullets)
- What is signed: manifest + bundle contents (hashes).
- What changes for customers: new verification step, new error codes, new break-glass policy.
- How to update trust store in air-gapped: file-based update, versioning, and recommended maintenance cadence.
- How to handle time skew: recommended time source, diagnostic override only (documented).

Support readiness items (must be complete before LA)
- Runbook: verification failures triage, decision tree, and log collection paths.
- FAQ + error code table (customer-facing).
- Template for support response for:
  - hash mismatch after transfer
  - unknown signing key after rotation
  - not-yet-valid/expired validity window (time skew)
  - downgrade attempt blocked
- Support bundle: includes bundle manifest + verification result + key id.
- Break-glass workflow: who approves, what to collect, and post-incident follow-up steps.

Metrics / Success metrics
- Pilot success rate: 100% installs succeed when bundle is intact and environment meets prerequisites.
- Verification failure diagnostics: support can identify root cause within 1 business day in 90% of cases (pilot/LA).
- Supply-chain confidence: customers accept signing approach in security review without requiring custom root in initial phase.
- Operational: signing pipeline SLOs met (time-to-issue signed bundle, low flake rate), and release gating prevents unsigned artifacts.

Risks / Open questions
- Air-gapped time sources vary; we need crisp guidance and minimal “time dependency” for verification (diagnostic-only overrides are acceptable but must be logged).
- Key rotation communication: how we ensure customers update trust store before they receive bundles signed with new key.
- Backward compatibility: transition from unsigned bundles for existing installations; ensure migration path is documented and safe.

- Rollout stage definitions and dates align to release train and gating.
